extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO (particularly those practicing trademark and other non-patent law), disciplinary counsel, USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing reciprocal disciplinary proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including grounds for imposing a suspension identical to state-court discipline and related duties during suspension and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline may file a "Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24" requesting the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A "Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24" must be sent (here by certified mail) providing the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If the respondent fails to file a response, the OED may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was suspended for sixty (60) days from practice before the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension was predicated upon the respondent being suspended for sixty (60) days from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State; such state suspension can form the basis for a § 11.804(h) violation leading to reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of public notice (Official Gazette) and notice to agencies per 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 & 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette about the suspension and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notice must state the respondent's name, the USPTO practice areas affected (e.g., trademark and non-patent matters), the underlying regulation violated, and a summary of the state-court suspensions and factual findings that predicate the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not recite § 11.58's text, the Order requires the respondent to observe the regulatory duties applicable during suspension (e.g., client notifications, cessation of practice as specified by § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with reinstatement requirements in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement procedures and any conditions therein must be satisfied by the respondent when seeking reinstatement before the USPTO; the Order conditions future reinstatement on full compliance with § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent conflict of interest (Iowa Rule 32:1.7(a)(2); Missouri Rule 4-1.7(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State rules cited (Iowa Rule 32:1.7(a)(2) and Missouri Rule 4-1.7(a)(2)) preclude an attorney from representing a client if the representation would involve a concurrent conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court of Iowa found that Willey's representation involved a concurrent conflict between clients (e.g., Synergy and Wieniewitz). Representing clients with concurrent conflicts without appropriate measures can constitute professional misconduct leading to suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent, confirmed in writing (Iowa Rule 32:1.7(b)(4); Missouri Rule 4-1.7(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a concurrent conflict of interest exists, one required step to cure the conflict is to obtain 'informed consent, confirmed in writing' from the affected clients (Iowa Rule 32:1.7(b)(4); Missouri Rule 4-1.7(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain written informed consent (and failure to, for example, recommend obtaining independent counsel) was a basis for the state suspensions and thus for reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of client funds and disclosure of client relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts found by the Iowa Supreme Court included: the attorney deposited a client's $100,000 check into the attorney trust account and immediately disbursed the money to another client/entity (Synergy); failed to inform the lending client that Synergy was a client of the attorney; did not obtain informed consent; did not recommend independent counsel; and loan payments were not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such handling and failures to disclose and obtain consent were treated as professional misconduct (violations of the cited state rules) and support suspension; attorneys must properly safeguard client funds, disclose relevant client relationships, and obtain consent when conflicts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED makes disciplinary decisions publicly accessible to promote transparency; practitioners and the public can consult the Reading Room for precedents and details of disciplinary actions.
